# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `python -m kindi.config_reference`; do not edit this file by hand. -->

Every setting Kindi reads, taken from the code itself: the config keys and their defaults from
`kindi/config.py` (`config.DEFAULTS`), and every `KINDI_*` environment variable read under
`kindi/`. `tests/test_config_reference.py` fails when either list changes and this file is not
regenerated.

Precedence (later wins): built-in defaults < config file < environment (`KINDI_<KEY>`) <
command-line flags. `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` is the prose guide, with the notes on the commonly
used switches.

Regenerate with:

```sh
python -m kindi.config_reference
```

## Config keys

Each key can also be set from the environment as `KINDI_<KEY>` (for example `KINDI_CTX=8192`).

### where things live

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pack` | path | `~/.kindi/pack` | the converted model (kindi convert) |
| `state_dir` | path | `~/.kindi/state` | saved prompt openings, head mode, kernel cache |

### server

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | string | `127.0.0.1` | 0.0.0.0 to serve the LAN |
| `port` | int | `8093` |  |
| `api_key` | string | (empty) | if set, clients must send Authorization: Bearer <api_key> |
| `model_name` | string | `auto` | infer the reported id from the selected pack |

### engine

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ctx` | int | `24576` | requested context; each backend clamps it to available device memory |
| `head` | string | `exact` | exact \| fast (shortlist head, ~15% faster, approximate) |
| `fast_clusters` | int | `256` | clusters scored by the fast head |

### prompt cache

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checkpoint_every` | int | `256` | recurrent-state checkpoint spacing (tokens) |
| `prefix_max` | int | `8` | saved prompt openings kept on disk |
| `prefix_min` | int | `512` | smallest opening worth saving (tokens) |
| `park_max` | int | `3` | other conversations kept in host RAM |
| `checkpoint_budget_mb` | int | `0` | host RAM for checkpoints and parked conversations (0: 20% of the RAM) |
| `repeat_stop` | int | `0` | 1: stop a reply caught in a repeating loop (close it while thinking) |
| `lookup` | int | `5` | Nanbeige: prompt-lookup drafting, up to this many tokens per check (0: off) |
| `mtp_head` | string | (empty) | Nanbeige: an MTP head file, a second draft source (empty: none) |
| `reasoning_effort` | string | (empty) | 27B template: xhigh \| medium \| low (empty: the template default, xhigh) |

### generation defaults (a request's own values win)

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_tokens` | int | `1024` |  |
| `temperature` | float | `0.7` |  |
| `top_p` | float | `0.8` |  |
| `top_k` | int | `20` |  |
| `min_p` | float | `0` | 0: off; else drop the tokens below min_p times the best one's probability |
| `repeat_penalty` | float | `1.0` | 1.0: off; llama.cpp's repeat penalty (the output is then not token-exact) |
| `repeat_last_n` | int | `64` | the tokens that repeat_penalty looks at (-1: the whole context) |
| `presence_penalty` | float | `0` | OpenAI's additive presence penalty: -2..2, 0 = off (Bonsai backends) |
| `sampling_profile` | string | `default` | default \| publisher: the model publisher's sampling values (Bonsai only) |
